chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Yaqoub, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about marriage without a sermon (khutbah), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Are not the majority of our youths marrying, and we are biting/eating the food on the table, saying,
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage without a formal sermon in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the simplicity of marriage contracts by citing the prevalent custom ('urf) of the Shia community, where a casual request during a meal suffices to formalize the union. This hadith underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the essence of marriage lies in the mutual consent and declaration (ijab wa qabul) rather than rigid ceremonial formalities, reflecting the flexibility of early Shia social practices.
